reasons: **We get the most important work done without crossing the heat limit, but only just.** This plan finishes about 62% of the high-priority work. Even our hottest workers should stay under the 38.0 °C body-temperature limit, but the closest call is less than a tenth of a degree away, so there's almost no room for surprises like a hotter day or a slow break.
**Pushing harder buys us nothing.** The plan built purely for speed gets the same 62% of the work done but runs people slightly hotter. There's no reason to choose it over this one.

**Spreading the work more evenly is a little safer but costs some output.** That option keeps people slightly cooler, but the gain is tiny (about 0.02 °C) and we'd finish only about 58% of the priority work. It's worth switching if conditions look hotter than expected or anyone on the crew is already struggling.

Hard safety rules:
- Every worker's 90th percentile core temperature must stay below 38.0 °C all shift. Harder work, sun and high WBGT heat people up; 30-min shade rests cool them down.
- Breaks: at most 3 work slots in a row, then a 'rest' slot; at most 2 in a row if any of those slots has WBGT >= 30.0 °C.
- No outdoor tasks during hazards that stop outdoor work. After lightning, outdoor work stays stopped for 30 more minutes.
- Workers who are not acclimatized never do very_heavy tasks when WBGT >= 28.0 °C.
Validity: one entry per slot per worker; off-site workers rest; skills and allowed slots must match.
